description: XiaoMiTool V2: modding tool for Xiaomi, Redmi and POCO phones: bootloader unlock, MIUI, Xiaomi.eu and custom ROM install, TWRP, Magisk root, unbrick. Abandoned upstream (last release 2020).
notes: Upstream is abandoned: 20.7.28 beta (July 2020) is the last release. Much of the tool talks to
Xiaomi's servers (login, unlock, ROM lists) and to xiaomitool.com, so parts may no longer work,
especially on HyperOS. Xiaomi's unlock rules (waiting time, Xiaomi Community app) still apply.
XiaoMiTool asks for administrator rights on start (UAC): it installs Android USB drivers itself.
Its adb and fastboot (in res\tools) are custom builds for MIUI and stay off the PATH.
Settings, logs, the saved Xiaomi session (if 'save session' is on), downloaded ROMs and their
extracted files all go to res\tmp, which is persisted in
ROMs take several GB each: delete them there by hand, or choose another download folder in Settings.
Decline the tool's own update offer: it would replace XiaoMiTool.jar inside the Scoop folder.
On start it sends its version and a hashed PC ID to xiaomitool.com to check for updates.
pre_install: # The NSIS installer is unpacked with 7-Zip instead of run: drop its plugins and uninstaller.
# A copy from upstream's installer is a separate portable folder: Scoop neither touches nor removes it,
# but it keeps its own settings and downloads, so say it is there.
$other = Get-ChildItem $roots -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Get-ItemProperty -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Where-Object { $_.DisplayName -like '*XiaoMiTool*' } | Select-Object -First 1

warn "XiaoMiTool is also installed with upstream's installer ($($where -replace [regex]::Escape($env:USERPROFILE), '%USERPROFILE%')). The two copies do not share settings or downloads; uninstall that one in Settings > Apps if you no longer need it."
